A nurse is reviewing the history of a 68-year-old client who recently retired and now reports falls and memory loss. The partner reports new urinary incontinence. Which action by the nurse is most appropriate?

  • A. Conclude that the changes are normal aging
  • B. Ask open-ended questions about alcohol and substance use
  • C. Request an antidepressant prescription
  • D. Instruct the partner to limit fluids
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Retirement and loss are stressors that can start alcohol or substance use in older adults, and falls, memory loss, and incontinence can be signs of alcohol use. Older adults show effects at lower doses. The nurse should use open-ended, nonjudgmental questions rather than assume normal aging.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has bulimia nervosa, purging type. Which laboratory finding should the nurse expect? A. Hyperkalemia B. Hypokalemia C. Hypernatremia D. Hypermagnesemia
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who has bulimia nervosa, purging type. Which laboratory finding should the nurse expect?

  • A. Hyperkalemia
  • B. Hypokalemia
  • C. Hypernatremia
  • D. Hypermagnesemia
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Purging by vomiting causes direct potassium loss, and dehydration raises aldosterone, which promotes potassium excretion. Hypokalemia with ECG changes such as a prolonged QT interval is the expected finding. Other imbalances in purging include hyponatremia and hypochloremia, while malnutrition causes hypomagnesemia, not hypermagnesemia.

cards.prompt: A nurse is planning care for a client who has anorexia nervosa. Which interventions should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. Monitor the client during and after meals B. Keep snacks at the bedside so the client can eat whenever hungry C. Use a behavioral contract with rewards for completing meals D. Provide small, frequent meals E. Offer coffee between meals to increase energy
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is planning care for a client who has anorexia nervosa. Which interventions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. Monitor the client during and after meals
  • B. Keep snacks at the bedside so the client can eat whenever hungry
  • C. Use a behavioral contract with rewards for completing meals
  • D. Provide small, frequent meals
  • E. Offer coffee between meals to increase energy
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D

Monitoring during and after meals prevents purging; contracts with rewards promote positive behavior; small frequent meals are tolerated better. A structured, inflexible schedule that permits food only at set times is used at the start of therapy, and caffeine should be avoided because it increases energy and difficulty controlling behaviors and can substitute for food.

cards.prompt: A client who has anorexia nervosa is admitted and started on nutritional support after severe malnutrition. Which finding should the nurse report immediately? A. Weight gain of 0.5 lb in 24 hours B. Heart rate of 38/min with new dysrhythmia C. Complaint of mild constipation D. Refusal to eat dessert
cards.promptHtml:
A client who has anorexia nervosa is admitted and started on nutritional support after severe malnutrition. Which finding should the nurse report immediately?

  • A. Weight gain of 0.5 lb in 24 hours
  • B. Heart rate of 38/min with new dysrhythmia
  • C. Complaint of mild constipation
  • D. Refusal to eat dessert
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Refeeding syndrome can cause dysrhythmias, severe bradycardia, and hypotension and can be fatal. These need continuous cardiac monitoring and prompt reporting to the provider. Mild constipation is managed with a high-fiber diet, a small weight gain is expected, and food refusal is a behavioral concern that is not an emergency.

cards.prompt: A client who has bulimia nervosa tells the nurse, "I know I look huge since I stopped throwing up. Everyone sees it." Which cognitive distortion does this statement most reflect? A. Catastrophizing B. All-or-nothing thinking C. Personalization D. Overgeneralization
cards.promptHtml:
A client who has bulimia nervosa tells the nurse, "I know I look huge since I stopped throwing up. Everyone sees it." Which cognitive distortion does this statement most reflect?

  • A. Catastrophizing
  • B. All-or-nothing thinking
  • C. Personalization
  • D. Overgeneralization
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Believing that everyone is looking at and judging the client's body is personalization, as in the example of walking through a hallway and assuming everyone is staring. Catastrophizing is predicting disaster ("my life is over"), all-or-nothing is extreme either-or thinking, and overgeneralization draws broad conclusions from one view.

cards.prompt: A client who has somatic symptom disorder reports a new onset of severe abdominal pain. What should the nurse do first? A. Tell the client that the pain is caused by stress B. Report the new symptom to the provider C. Remind the client of the time limit for discussing symptoms D. Teach assertiveness techniques
cards.promptHtml:
A client who has somatic symptom disorder reports a new onset of severe abdominal pain. What should the nurse do first?

  • A. Tell the client that the pain is caused by stress
  • B. Report the new symptom to the provider
  • C. Remind the client of the time limit for discussing symptoms
  • D. Teach assertiveness techniques
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

New physical symptoms in a client who has somatic symptom disorder must be reported to the provider because they can have a real physical cause. Telling the client it is stress dismisses the client's experience. Time limits and assertiveness teaching are appropriate parts of the plan but do not address a possible acute problem.

cards.prompt: A nurse is collecting data from a client who has conversion disorder. Which findings are consistent with the disorder? Select all that apply. A. Sudden loss of voice after an argument B. Absence of any neurologic diagnosis to explain the loss C. Calm lack of concern about the symptom D. Intentional falsification of symptoms to obtain money E. Deficit in voluntary sensory function
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is collecting data from a client who has conversion disorder. Which findings are consistent with the disorder? Select all that apply.

  • A. Sudden loss of voice after an argument
  • B. Absence of any neurologic diagnosis to explain the loss
  • C. Calm lack of concern about the symptom
  • D. Intentional falsification of symptoms to obtain money
  • E. Deficit in voluntary sensory function
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, E

Conversion disorder involves loss of voluntary motor or sensory function (such as aphonia) after emotional stress, without a neurologic cause, and some clients show la belle indifference. Intentionally faking symptoms for money is malingering, which is consciously motivated by personal gain and is not a mental illness.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who frequently describes symptoms using precise medical terms, reports new symptoms after tests are normal, and does not want the provider to talk to prior providers. The nurse suspects factitious disorder. Which action is best? A. Confront the client about faking symptoms B. Ignore the suspicion to preserve rapport C. Share the suspicion openly with the health care team D. Discharge the client immediately
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who frequently describes symptoms using precise medical terms, reports new symptoms after tests are normal, and does not want the provider to talk to prior providers. The nurse suspects factitious disorder. Which action is best?

  • A. Confront the client about faking symptoms
  • B. Ignore the suspicion to preserve rapport
  • C. Share the suspicion openly with the health care team
  • D. Discharge the client immediately
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

The nurse should avoid confrontation and communicate suspicions of factitious disorder openly with the team, which can reduce medical cost and unnecessary treatments or procedures. The nurse should also do a self-assessment and keep the client safe. Confrontation damages trust, ignoring the concern risks harm, and discharge is not a nursing decision.

cards.prompt: A nurse is comparing two clients. Client 1 admits exaggerating back pain so that a military deployment will be cancelled. Client 2 secretly adds medication to an older parent's food so that staff will praise the client's devoted caregiving. Which statement by the nurse is accurate? A. "Client 1 is likely malingering and client 2 is likely to have factitious disorder imposed on another." B. "Both clients have somatic symptom disorder." C. "Client 1 has conversion disorder and client 2 has illness anxiety disorder." D. "Both clients are malingering."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is comparing two clients. Client 1 admits exaggerating back pain so that a military deployment will be cancelled. Client 2 secretly adds medication to an older parent's food so that staff will praise the client's devoted caregiving. Which statement by the nurse is accurate?

  • A. "Client 1 is likely malingering and client 2 is likely to have factitious disorder imposed on another."
  • B. "Both clients have somatic symptom disorder."
  • C. "Client 1 has conversion disorder and client 2 has illness anxiety disorder."
  • D. "Both clients are malingering."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Malingering is consciously motivated by personal gain, such as evading military service, and is not a mental illness. Factitious disorder imposed on another involves deliberately making a vulnerable person ill for attention or relief of responsibility, so the parent's safety must be protected. Somatic symptom, conversion, and illness anxiety disorders are not consciously produced.

cards.prompt: A nurse is monitoring a client who received IV lorazepam 20 min ago for severe agitation. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider immediately? A. Respiratory rate of 8/min and blood pressure 82/46 mm Hg B. Client states, "I can't remember what you just told me." C. Client is drowsy but answers questions appropriately D. Client reports mild lightheadedness when sitting up
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is monitoring a client who received IV lorazepam 20 min ago for severe agitation. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider immediately?

  • A. Respiratory rate of 8/min and blood pressure 82/46 mm Hg
  • B. Client states, "I can't remember what you just told me."
  • C. Client is drowsy but answers questions appropriately
  • D. Client reports mild lightheadedness when sitting up
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

IV benzodiazepine toxicity causes respiratory depression, severe hypotension, and cardiac arrest. Airway, breathing, and circulation come first: maintain a patent airway, support blood pressure with IV fluids, have resuscitation equipment ready, and expect flumazenil to reverse sedation. Anterograde amnesia, drowsiness, and lightheadedness are expected CNS effects to monitor and report, but they are not immediately life-threatening.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for buspirone for generalized anxiety disorder. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. "You should take this medication every day, not only when you feel anxious." B. "Avoid drinking grapefruit juice." C. "This medication will make you drowsy, so do not drive." D. "Tell the provider before taking any medication for depression such as an MAOI." E. "You might develop withdrawal symptoms if you miss a dose."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for buspirone for generalized anxiety disorder. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. "You should take this medication every day, not only when you feel anxious."
  • B. "Avoid drinking grapefruit juice."
  • C. "This medication will make you drowsy, so do not drive."
  • D. "Tell the provider before taking any medication for depression such as an MAOI."
  • E. "You might develop withdrawal symptoms if you miss a dose."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D

Buspirone has a slow onset and must be taken on a schedule. Grapefruit juice, erythromycin and ketoconazole raise its effects. It is contraindicated with MAOIs (hypertensive crisis) and for 14 days after stopping them. It does not cause sedation, and tolerance, dependence and withdrawal are not concerns.

cards.prompt: A client who takes sertraline tells the nurse they started taking St. John's wort for their mood 2 days ago. Which group of findings should the nurse report to the provider? A. Dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention B. Bradycardia, low body temperature, and muscle flaccidity C. Weight gain and decreased sexual interest D. Fever, hyperreflexia, diaphoresis, and agitation
cards.promptHtml:
A client who takes sertraline tells the nurse they started taking St. John's wort for their mood 2 days ago. Which group of findings should the nurse report to the provider?

  • A. Dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention
  • B. Bradycardia, low body temperature, and muscle flaccidity
  • C. Weight gain and decreased sexual interest
  • D. Fever, hyperreflexia, diaphoresis, and agitation
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Concurrent use of an SSRI with St. John's wort, TCAs, or MAOIs can cause serotonin syndrome, which can begin 2 to 72 hr after the combination starts and can be lethal. Findings include agitation, hallucinations, diaphoresis, hyperreflexia, tachycardia, and fever. Dry mouth and constipation are anticholinergic effects. Serotonin syndrome causes tachycardia and hyperthermia, not bradycardia and low temperature. Weight gain and sexual dysfunction are later SSRI effects, not an emergency.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the medication list of an older adult client who takes furosemide and has a new prescription for sertraline. Which laboratory value should the nurse monitor? A. Serum potassium only B. Serum sodium C. Serum calcium D. Serum lithium level
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the medication list of an older adult client who takes furosemide and has a new prescription for sertraline. Which laboratory value should the nurse monitor?

  • A. Serum potassium only
  • B. Serum sodium
  • C. Serum calcium
  • D. Serum lithium level
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

SSRIs can cause hyponatremia, which is more likely in older adults who take diuretics. ATI directs the nurse to obtain a baseline sodium and monitor it periodically throughout treatment. Potassium and calcium are not the specified SSRI concern, and the client is not on lithium.

cards.prompt: A nurse is teaching a client who takes alprazolam. Which statements by the client indicate understanding? Select all that apply. A. "I will not drink alcohol while taking this medication." B. "I can stop taking this medicine all at once if I feel better." C. "I will not chew the sustained-release tablets." D. "I will keep this medicine in a secure place." E. "I should report confusion to my provider."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is teaching a client who takes alprazolam. Which statements by the client indicate understanding? Select all that apply.

  • A. "I will not drink alcohol while taking this medication."
  • B. "I can stop taking this medicine all at once if I feel better."
  • C. "I will not chew the sustained-release tablets."
  • D. "I will keep this medicine in a secure place."
  • E. "I should report confusion to my provider."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D, E

Alcohol with benzodiazepines causes CNS and respiratory depression. Sustained-release tablets are swallowed whole. Benzodiazepines have misuse potential and should be stored securely. Confusion can indicate toxicity. Abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal (anxiety, tremors, delirium, seizures), so the dose must be tapered over several weeks after long-term use.

cards.prompt: A provider plans to switch a client from fluoxetine to phenelzine. The nurse should reinforce that fluoxetine must be discontinued for how long before phenelzine is started? A. 24 hr B. 72 hr C. 5 weeks D. 6 months
cards.promptHtml:
A provider plans to switch a client from fluoxetine to phenelzine. The nurse should reinforce that fluoxetine must be discontinued for how long before phenelzine is started?

  • A. 24 hr
  • B. 72 hr
  • C. 5 weeks
  • D. 6 months
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Fluoxetine has a long effective half-life, so ATI states it should be discontinued 5 weeks before an MAOI such as phenelzine is started. Starting the MAOI sooner risks serotonin syndrome. In the other direction, an MAOI is stopped 14 days before an SSRI or SNRI is started. Shorter washouts are unsafe, and 6 months is not required.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who takes phenelzine. The client reports a severe headache, palpitations, and nausea after eating dinner at a restaurant. The client's blood pressure is 210/118 mm Hg. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Notify the provider and the RN of a possible hypertensive crisis. B. Administer a PRN acetaminophen. C. Encourage the client to rest in a quiet room. D. Ask the client to list what was eaten.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who takes phenelzine. The client reports a severe headache, palpitations, and nausea after eating dinner at a restaurant. The client's blood pressure is 210/118 mm Hg. Which action should the nurse take first?

  • A. Notify the provider and the RN of a possible hypertensive crisis.
  • B. Administer a PRN acetaminophen.
  • C. Encourage the client to rest in a quiet room.
  • D. Ask the client to list what was eaten.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Headache, nausea, increased heart rate and markedly elevated blood pressure after a possible tyramine exposure indicate hypertensive crisis, an emergency. The nurse notifies the provider and RN immediately and assists with phentolamine IV or nifedipine and cardiac monitoring. Analgesics and resting delay treatment. Diet history is useful afterward.

cards.prompt: A nurse is teaching a client who has a new prescription for phenelzine. Which foods or substances should the nurse tell the client to avoid? Select all that apply. A. Aged cheese B. Cooked fresh vegetables C. Salami D. Red wine E. Chocolate
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is teaching a client who has a new prescription for phenelzine. Which foods or substances should the nurse tell the client to avoid? Select all that apply.

  • A. Aged cheese
  • B. Cooked fresh vegetables
  • C. Salami
  • D. Red wine
  • E. Chocolate
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D, E

MAOIs prevent breakdown of tyramine, so aged cheese, pepperoni, salami, avocados, figs, bananas, smoked fish, some beers and red wine can cause hypertensive crisis. Caffeine and chocolate also contain pressor agents. Cooked fresh vegetables are not on the restricted list. Written instructions should be reinforced.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the health history of a client who has a new prescription for bupropion for depression. Which finding is the priority to report to the provider? A. Takes ibuprofen occasionally for back pain B. Reports low energy and poor concentration C. Has a current diagnosis of bulimia nervosa D. Previously stopped an SSRI because of decreased libido
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the health history of a client who has a new prescription for bupropion for depression. Which finding is the priority to report to the provider?

  • A. Takes ibuprofen occasionally for back pain
  • B. Reports low energy and poor concentration
  • C. Has a current diagnosis of bulimia nervosa
  • D. Previously stopped an SSRI because of decreased libido
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa, as well as in seizure disorders and with MAOIs. It should also be avoided in clients at risk for seizures, such as after a head injury. Low energy and poor concentration are manifestations of the depression being treated. Bupropion is an alternative for clients who could not tolerate SSRI sexual adverse effects. Occasional ibuprofen is not a stated bupropion concern.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who takes amitriptyline and reports dry mouth and difficulty urinating. Which instruction is most appropriate? A. "Limit your fluid intake after dinner." B. "Void just before taking the medication and chew sugarless gum." C. "Take the medication with grapefruit juice." D. "Stop the medication until the symptoms resolve."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who takes amitriptyline and reports dry mouth and difficulty urinating. Which instruction is most appropriate?

  • A. "Limit your fluid intake after dinner."
  • B. "Void just before taking the medication and chew sugarless gum."
  • C. "Take the medication with grapefruit juice."
  • D. "Stop the medication until the symptoms resolve."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

TCAs have anticholinergic effects. Voiding before the dose reduces urinary hesitancy or retention; sugarless gum and sips of water relieve dry mouth. Fluids should be maintained, not restricted. The client must not stop the drug abruptly; notify the provider if effects persist.

cards.prompt: A nurse is assisting in the care of a client who is receiving fluoxetine. Which findings should the nurse report as indications of serotonin syndrome? Select all that apply. A. Hyperreflexia B. Bradycardia C. Diaphoresis D. Agitation E. Hypothermia
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is assisting in the care of a client who is receiving fluoxetine. Which findings should the nurse report as indications of serotonin syndrome? Select all that apply.

  • A. Hyperreflexia
  • B. Bradycardia
  • C. Diaphoresis
  • D. Agitation
  • E. Hypothermia
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D

Serotonin syndrome includes agitation, diaphoresis, hyperreflexia, tremors, incoordination, confusion, hallucinations, diarrhea, and fever. Heart rate rises (tachycardia) and temperature rises (hyperpyrexia), so bradycardia and hypothermia are incorrect. Withhold the medication and notify the provider.

cards.prompt: A nurse is planning care for a client who is being discharged on a new SSRI after hospitalization for major depression. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching? A. "I will take the medication every morning." B. "I will call if I notice bleeding or black stools." C. "I may stop the medication when my mood improves." D. "It can take several weeks to feel the full effect."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is planning care for a client who is being discharged on a new SSRI after hospitalization for major depression. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?

  • A. "I will take the medication every morning."
  • B. "I will call if I notice bleeding or black stools."
  • C. "I may stop the medication when my mood improves."
  • D. "It can take several weeks to feel the full effect."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Therapy continues after improvement, usually for months and sometimes a year or longer. Sudden discontinuation can cause relapse or withdrawal, so a taper is required. Morning dosing limits sleep disturbance, bleeding is a risk, and the delayed onset is expected.

cards.prompt: A client who takes lithium carbonate calls the clinic and reports vomiting and diarrhea for the past 2 days. Which instruction should the nurse give? A. "Take an extra dose today to replace what you lost by vomiting." B. "Hold your lithium and get medical care today." C. "Drink less fluid until the diarrhea stops." D. "Cut back on salt until your stomach settles."
cards.promptHtml:
A client who takes lithium carbonate calls the clinic and reports vomiting and diarrhea for the past 2 days. Which instruction should the nurse give?

  • A. "Take an extra dose today to replace what you lost by vomiting."
  • B. "Hold your lithium and get medical care today."
  • C. "Drink less fluid until the diarrhea stops."
  • D. "Cut back on salt until your stomach settles."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Vomiting, diarrhea, and excessive sweating deplete fluid and sodium, which decreases lithium excretion and can cause toxicity. ATI instructs the client to withhold the medication and seek medical attention when these occur. An extra dose raises the toxicity risk. Clients should keep fluid intake at 1.5 to 3 L/day and keep sodium intake adequate, so restricting fluid or salt is wrong.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for lithium carbonate. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. "Keep your salt intake steady." B. "Drink at least 1.5 to 3 liters of fluid each day." C. "Stop the medication if you have a fine hand tremor." D. "Hold the medication and call if you have vomiting or diarrhea." E. "Lithium levels are checked 10 to 12 hours after your last dose."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for lithium carbonate. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. "Keep your salt intake steady."
  • B. "Drink at least 1.5 to 3 liters of fluid each day."
  • C. "Stop the medication if you have a fine hand tremor."
  • D. "Hold the medication and call if you have vomiting or diarrhea."
  • E. "Lithium levels are checked 10 to 12 hours after your last dose."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

Sodium and fluid balance keep lithium levels stable. Vomiting, diarrhea, and heavy sweating can precipitate toxicity. Blood is drawn in the morning 10 to 12 hr after the last dose. A mild fine tremor is a common adverse effect and is not a reason to stop; the client should report an increase.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who takes lithium and has a serum lithium level of 2.2 mEq/L, tinnitus, and blurred vision. Which action should the nurse anticipate? A. Administer the next dose. B. Give a thiazide diuretic. C. Repeat the level in one week. D. Prepare for gastric lavage or measures to increase excretion.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who takes lithium and has a serum lithium level of 2.2 mEq/L, tinnitus, and blurred vision. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

  • A. Administer the next dose.
  • B. Give a thiazide diuretic.
  • C. Repeat the level in one week.
  • D. Prepare for gastric lavage or measures to increase excretion.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

A level of 2.0 to 2.5 mEq/L with tinnitus, blurred vision, and other CNS findings is advanced toxicity. Treatment includes emetic or gastric lavage and urea, mannitol, or aminophylline to increase excretion; care is in an acute setting, and hemodialysis may be needed above 2.5. Diuretics raise lithium levels.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing monitoring for a client who has a new prescription for valproate. Which should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. Liver function tests B. Amylase level C. Platelet count D. Thyroid-stimulating hormone annually E. Serum valproic acid level
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing monitoring for a client who has a new prescription for valproate. Which should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. Liver function tests
  • B. Amylase level
  • C. Platelet count
  • D. Thyroid-stimulating hormone annually
  • E. Serum valproic acid level
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, E

Valproate can cause hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and thrombocytopenia, and the therapeutic level is 50 to 120 mcg/mL. Annual thyroid testing is specific to lithium.

cards.prompt: A client who takes carbamazepine for rapid cycling bipolar disorder reports fever, sore throat, and bruising. The nurse should recognize these as indications of which adverse effect? A. Hypoosmolarity B. Hepatotoxicity C. Pancreatitis D. Blood dyscrasias
cards.promptHtml:
A client who takes carbamazepine for rapid cycling bipolar disorder reports fever, sore throat, and bruising. The nurse should recognize these as indications of which adverse effect?

  • A. Hypoosmolarity
  • B. Hepatotoxicity
  • C. Pancreatitis
  • D. Blood dyscrasias
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Carbamazepine can cause leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. Infection signs and bruising or gum bleeding need immediate provider notification. Hypoosmolarity presents with edema, decreased urine output, and hypertension. Hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis are valproate concerns.

cards.prompt: A client who takes lamotrigine and an oral contraceptive reports a new red rash on the trunk. Which action is the priority? A. Apply an antihistamine cream and recheck in 24 hours. B. Wear sunscreen and continue the medication. C. Withhold the medication and notify the provider. D. Increase fluid intake.
cards.promptHtml:
A client who takes lamotrigine and an oral contraceptive reports a new red rash on the trunk. Which action is the priority?

  • A. Apply an antihistamine cream and recheck in 24 hours.
  • B. Wear sunscreen and continue the medication.
  • C. Withhold the medication and notify the provider.
  • D. Increase fluid intake.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Lamotrigine can cause serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome. ATI directs withholding the medication and notifying the provider. Slow titration reduces risk. Oral contraceptives also reduce lamotrigine effect, so the client needs another form of birth control.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who takes haloperidol and suddenly develops severe spasms of the neck and tongue. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Obtain a CBC. B. Stay with the client, monitor the airway, and notify the provider for benztropine. C. Apply cooling blankets. D. Administer an antihistamine PO and observe.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who takes haloperidol and suddenly develops severe spasms of the neck and tongue. Which action should the nurse take first?

  • A. Obtain a CBC.
  • B. Stay with the client, monitor the airway, and notify the provider for benztropine.
  • C. Apply cooling blankets.
  • D. Administer an antihistamine PO and observe.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Severe spasm of the tongue, neck, face, or back is acute dystonia, a crisis. Stay with the client, protect the airway, and obtain an order for benztropine or IM/IV diphenhydramine. A CBC is for agranulocytosis and cooling blankets are for NMS. Oral medication is too slow.

cards.prompt: A nurse is assisting with care of a client who has neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply. A. Stop the antipsychotic medication. B. Apply cooling blankets. C. Restrict fluids. D. Prepare to administer dantrolene or bromocriptine. E. Assist with transfer to the ICU.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is assisting with care of a client who has neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

  • A. Stop the antipsychotic medication.
  • B. Apply cooling blankets.
  • C. Restrict fluids.
  • D. Prepare to administer dantrolene or bromocriptine.
  • E. Assist with transfer to the ICU.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

NMS is a life-threatening emergency: stop the drug, monitor vital signs, cool the client, give antipyretics, increase fluids, give dantrolene or bromocriptine for muscle relaxation, treat arrhythmias, and transfer to ICU. Fluids should be increased, not restricted. Resume only after 2 weeks, consider an atypical agent.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has started clozapine. Which instruction should the nurse include? A. "Your white blood cell count will be checked on a set schedule, and you should report fever or sore throat." B. "You will need annual blood counts." C. "Clozapine has no risk of weight gain." D. "Expect your blood pressure to rise."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who has started clozapine. Which instruction should the nurse include?

  • A. "Your white blood cell count will be checked on a set schedule, and you should report fever or sore throat."
  • B. "You will need annual blood counts."
  • C. "Clozapine has no risk of weight gain."
  • D. "Expect your blood pressure to rise."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Clozapine carries a risk of fatal agranulocytosis, with WBC monitoring weekly, biweekly, then monthly. Infection signs (fever, sore throat, mouth lesions) must be reported. It also carries a high risk of weight gain, diabetes, and dyslipidemia, and it causes orthostatic hypotension.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing administration of antipsychotic medications. Which instructions are correct? Select all that apply. A. Give lurasidone with food (at least 350 kcal). B. Tell the client taking asenapine to swallow the tablet with water. C. Observe the client for at least 3 hr after olanzapine extended-release injection. D. Tell the client taking asenapine to avoid eating or drinking for 10 minutes after the dose. E. Give ziprasidone with food.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing administration of antipsychotic medications. Which instructions are correct? Select all that apply.

  • A. Give lurasidone with food (at least 350 kcal).
  • B. Tell the client taking asenapine to swallow the tablet with water.
  • C. Observe the client for at least 3 hr after olanzapine extended-release injection.
  • D. Tell the client taking asenapine to avoid eating or drinking for 10 minutes after the dose.
  • E. Give ziprasidone with food.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D, E

Lurasidone and ziprasidone are given with food to maximize absorption. Asenapine is a sublingual tablet that must not be swallowed; avoid food and drink for 10 minutes. Olanzapine extended-release injection requires observation for at least 3 hr.

cards.prompt: A client with schizophrenia who has taken perphenazine for 3 years has involuntary lip smacking and tongue movements. Which action should the nurse take? A. Administer benztropine. B. Report the findings and anticipate a dose reduction or switch to a second-generation antipsychotic. C. Tell the client the movements will resolve if the medication is stopped. D. Withhold all antipsychotics permanently.
cards.promptHtml:
A client with schizophrenia who has taken perphenazine for 3 years has involuntary lip smacking and tongue movements. Which action should the nurse take?

  • A. Administer benztropine.
  • B. Report the findings and anticipate a dose reduction or switch to a second-generation antipsychotic.
  • C. Tell the client the movements will resolve if the medication is stopped.
  • D. Withhold all antipsychotics permanently.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Lip smacking and tongue movements after months to years are tardive dyskinesia. The dose should be lowered or the client switched to a second-generation agent. TD usually does not decrease even with discontinuation and there is no reliable treatment. Benztropine treats early EPS, not TD.

cards.prompt: A nurse is planning care for a client who has a new prescription for olanzapine. Which laboratory value should the nurse plan to monitor? A. Lithium level B. Serum sodium C. Prothrombin time D. Fasting blood glucose
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is planning care for a client who has a new prescription for olanzapine. Which laboratory value should the nurse plan to monitor?

  • A. Lithium level
  • B. Serum sodium
  • C. Prothrombin time
  • D. Fasting blood glucose
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Olanzapine carries a high risk of diabetes, weight gain, and dyslipidemia (metabolic syndrome). ATI directs baseline fasting glucose with periodic monitoring, and cholesterol and triglycerides if weight gain is greater than 14 kg (31 lb). Lithium, sodium, and PT are not the key monitors for this drug.

cards.prompt: A nurse is teaching the parents of a 9-year-old who has ADHD and a new prescription for methylphenidate transdermal patches. Which instruction should the nurse include? A. "Put on a new patch each evening after supper." B. "Cut the patch in half if your child seems too sleepy." C. "Place the patch on the same hip each morning." D. "Remove the patch after 9 hours and flush it down the toilet."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is teaching the parents of a 9-year-old who has ADHD and a new prescription for methylphenidate transdermal patches. Which instruction should the nurse include?

  • A. "Put on a new patch each evening after supper."
  • B. "Cut the patch in half if your child seems too sleepy."
  • C. "Place the patch on the same hip each morning."
  • D. "Remove the patch after 9 hours and flush it down the toilet."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

The patch is applied once daily in the morning to a clean, dry hip, alternating hips, removed after no more than 9 hr, and flushed down the toilet to prevent others from using it. Evening application worsens insomnia, the same site is not used daily, and cutting a patch is not part of ATI teaching.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for an adolescent who has a new prescription for fluoxetine for major depressive disorder. Which of the following should the nurse include in teaching? Select all that apply. A. "Take the medication in the morning to reduce sleep problems." B. "Report any thoughts of harming yourself." C. "Stop the medication if you feel better after 2 weeks." D. "Avoid taking St. John's wort while on this medication." E. "Full effects may take up to 12 weeks."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for an adolescent who has a new prescription for fluoxetine for major depressive disorder. Which of the following should the nurse include in teaching? Select all that apply.

  • A. "Take the medication in the morning to reduce sleep problems."
  • B. "Report any thoughts of harming yourself."
  • C. "Stop the medication if you feel better after 2 weeks."
  • D. "Avoid taking St. John's wort while on this medication."
  • E. "Full effects may take up to 12 weeks."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

SSRIs are taken in the morning because they can cause insomnia. They can increase suicidal ideation in children and adolescents, so thoughts of self-harm are reported. St. John's wort with an SSRI can cause serotonin syndrome. Initial response occurs in 1 to 3 weeks with maximum effect by 12 weeks. Abrupt stopping causes discontinuation syndrome.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the prescription of a 12-year-old who has ADHD and is taking guanfacine. The nurse should recognize which of the following as the greatest risk if the parent stops the medication suddenly? A. Rebound hypertension B. Serotonin syndrome C. Hepatotoxicity D. Hallucinations
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the prescription of a 12-year-old who has ADHD and is taking guanfacine. The nurse should recognize which of the following as the greatest risk if the parent stops the medication suddenly?

  • A. Rebound hypertension
  • B. Serotonin syndrome
  • C. Hepatotoxicity
  • D. Hallucinations
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Alpha2-adrenergic agonists such as guanfacine and clonidine must be tapered on a schedule because abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound hypertension. Serotonin syndrome relates to serotonergic combinations, hepatotoxicity is associated with atomoxetine, and hallucinations are associated with stimulant toxicity or psychotic reactions.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for an adolescent who has autism spectrum disorder and a new prescription for risperidone. Which baseline assessment is the priority before therapy begins? A. Serum lithium level B. Serum sodium C. Fasting blood glucose D. Serum creatine kinase
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for an adolescent who has autism spectrum disorder and a new prescription for risperidone. Which baseline assessment is the priority before therapy begins?

  • A. Serum lithium level
  • B. Serum sodium
  • C. Fasting blood glucose
  • D. Serum creatine kinase
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Atypical antipsychotics can cause new-onset diabetes or loss of glucose control, so ATI directs a baseline fasting blood glucose with periodic monitoring. Lithium levels apply only to lithium therapy. Sodium and creatine kinase are not the ATI baseline for risperidone. Cholesterol and weight are also monitored.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client on day 3 of alcohol withdrawal who is severely disoriented, hallucinating, and has a blood pressure of 198/112 mm Hg. Which action is the priority? A. Provide a quiet room and dim the lights B. Offer fluids and a snack C. Encourage the client to attend a 12-step meeting D. Notify the provider immediately because this is a medical emergency
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client on day 3 of alcohol withdrawal who is severely disoriented, hallucinating, and has a blood pressure of 198/112 mm Hg. Which action is the priority?

  • A. Provide a quiet room and dim the lights
  • B. Offer fluids and a snack
  • C. Encourage the client to attend a 12-step meeting
  • D. Notify the provider immediately because this is a medical emergency
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Alcohol withdrawal delirium occurs 2 to 3 days after cessation, is a medical emergency, and can progress to death. Severe disorientation, hallucinations, severe hypertension, and dysrhythmias require immediate provider notification. Environmental measures help but do not come first. Twelve-step meetings apply to recovery, not an acute emergency.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for disulfiram. Which of the following statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. "Avoid cough syrup and mouthwash that contain alcohol." B. "Wear a medical alert bracelet." C. "You will have blood tests to check your liver." D. "A reaction to alcohol can still happen for up to 2 weeks after your last dose." E. "Your first dose will be given as soon as you stop drinking."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a client who has a new prescription for disulfiram. Which of the following statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. "Avoid cough syrup and mouthwash that contain alcohol."
  • B. "Wear a medical alert bracelet."
  • C. "You will have blood tests to check your liver."
  • D. "A reaction to alcohol can still happen for up to 2 weeks after your last dose."
  • E. "Your first dose will be given as soon as you stop drinking."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, D

Disulfiram causes acetaldehyde syndrome with even small amounts of alcohol, including hidden alcohol in products, so labels matter. A medical alert bracelet is advised, and the effect persists for 2 weeks after discontinuation. Liver function tests detect hepatotoxicity. The first dose is not given until 12 hr after the last drink.

cards.prompt: A nurse is preparing to give propranolol to a client during alcohol withdrawal. The client's apical pulse is 48/min. Which action should the nurse take? A. Administer the dose and recheck in 1 hr B. Administer half the dose C. Withhold the dose and notify the provider D. Give the dose with a snack
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is preparing to give propranolol to a client during alcohol withdrawal. The client's apical pulse is 48/min. Which action should the nurse take?

  • A. Administer the dose and recheck in 1 hr
  • B. Administer half the dose
  • C. Withhold the dose and notify the provider
  • D. Give the dose with a snack
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Beta blockers used to depress the autonomic response during withdrawal are held when the heart rate is below 50/min. The nurse withholds the dose and notifies the provider. Giving any dose risks symptomatic bradycardia.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who took an overdose of heroin and has slow, shallow respirations and is difficult to arouse. Which medication should the nurse anticipate administering? A. Naloxone B. Flumazenil C. Methadone D. Buprenorphine
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who took an overdose of heroin and has slow, shallow respirations and is difficult to arouse. Which medication should the nurse anticipate administering?

  • A. Naloxone
  • B. Flumazenil
  • C. Methadone
  • D. Buprenorphine
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Naloxone is the opioid antidote: a specific opioid antagonist that can be given IM, SQ, IV, or inhaled, and it reverses the slowed breathing, coma, and other effects of an opioid overdose. Flumazenil is the antidote for benzodiazepines. Methadone and buprenorphine are opioid substitution drugs and would add to the respiratory depression.

cards.prompt: A client whose partner was killed in a car crash 3 weeks ago tells the nurse, "If I had driven that night instead of him, none of this would have happened." Which response should the nurse make? A. "You did everything you could." B. "He is in a better place now." C. "It sounds like you are feeling guilty. Tell me more about how you are feeling." D. "Let's talk about something more pleasant for a while."
cards.promptHtml:
A client whose partner was killed in a car crash 3 weeks ago tells the nurse, "If I had driven that night instead of him, none of this would have happened." Which response should the nurse make?

  • A. "You did everything you could."
  • B. "He is in a better place now."
  • C. "It sounds like you are feeling guilty. Tell me more about how you are feeling."
  • D. "Let's talk about something more pleasant for a while."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Naming the emotion and inviting the client to talk is therapeutic. False reassurance, cliches such as "in a better place," and changing the subject block open expression of feelings. Guilt is an emotion that can occur in normal grief.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who is dying. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to protect against feelings of abandonment and isolation? Select all that apply. A. Answer call lights promptly B. Make frequent contact with the client C. Move the client to a room at the end of the hall for quiet D. Allow family members to stay with the client as much as possible E. Tell the client when procedures will occur
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a client who is dying. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to protect against feelings of abandonment and isolation? Select all that apply.

  • A. Answer call lights promptly
  • B. Make frequent contact with the client
  • C. Move the client to a room at the end of the hall for quiet
  • D. Allow family members to stay with the client as much as possible
  • E. Tell the client when procedures will occur
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

ATI lists prompt call light response, frequent contact, family presence, and informing the client of procedure times to lessen the fear of dying alone. The client should be placed where most comfortable, such as near the nurses' station, rather than an isolated room.

cards.prompt: A client states, "The doctor told me my cancer is terminal. If I just eat healthy and pray every day, maybe it will go away." The nurse recognizes this statement as which of Kubler-Ross's stages? A. Anger B. Acceptance C. Depression D. Bargaining
cards.promptHtml:
A client states, "The doctor told me my cancer is terminal. If I just eat healthy and pray every day, maybe it will go away." The nurse recognizes this statement as which of Kubler-Ross's stages?

  • A. Anger
  • B. Acceptance
  • C. Depression
  • D. Bargaining
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

In bargaining the client negotiates for more time or a cure. Anger is directed at self, others, or objects. Depression is overwhelming sadness at inability to change the situation. Acceptance involves accepting what is happening and planning for the future.

cards.prompt: A nurse is assessing a client 8 months after the death of a child. The client has stopped working, rarely leaves home, and says, "I am worthless and should have been the one who died." Which action is the priority? A. Encourage the client to attend a funeral anniversary event B. Assess the client for suicidal thoughts C. Explain that acceptance is expected by 6 months D. Suggest the client begin new relationships
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is assessing a client 8 months after the death of a child. The client has stopped working, rarely leaves home, and says, "I am worthless and should have been the one who died." Which action is the priority?

  • A. Encourage the client to attend a funeral anniversary event
  • B. Assess the client for suicidal thoughts
  • C. Explain that acceptance is expected by 6 months
  • D. Suggest the client begin new relationships
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Loss of self-esteem, worthlessness, and inability to function suggest complicated grief, which is associated with suicidal thoughts. Safety assessment comes first, followed by referral for psychotherapy. Educating about timeframes or encouraging new relationships does not address immediate risk.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a school-age child who has oppositional defiant disorder. Which statement by the child's guardian indicates understanding of the nurse's teaching? A. "I will let my child decide which rules to follow." B. "I will give a token each time my child follows a rule." C. "I will remove all limits so my child doesn't feel pressured." D. "I will punish my child with harsh discipline each time he argues."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a school-age child who has oppositional defiant disorder. Which statement by the child's guardian indicates understanding of the nurse's teaching?

  • A. "I will let my child decide which rules to follow."
  • B. "I will give a token each time my child follows a rule."
  • C. "I will remove all limits so my child doesn't feel pressured."
  • D. "I will punish my child with harsh discipline each time he argues."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

ATI recommends a reward system (wall chart or tokens), clear limits, consistency, and a calm, firm, respectful approach. Letting the child choose rules or removing limits fails to set limits. Harsh discipline is a contributing factor for conduct disorder and does not promote positive behavior.

cards.prompt: A nurse is assessing an adolescent who has conduct disorder. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply. A. Inflated self-esteem B. Intimidating classmates C. Lack of remorse for hurting others D. Suicidal ideation E. Truancy and running away
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is assessing an adolescent who has conduct disorder. Which findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.

  • A. Inflated self-esteem
  • B. Intimidating classmates
  • C. Lack of remorse for hurting others
  • D. Suicidal ideation
  • E. Truancy and running away
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B, C, D, E

Conduct disorder includes lack of remorse, bullying and threatening, suicidal ideation, running away, lying, shoplifting, and truancy. Clients with conduct disorder show low self-esteem, not inflated self-esteem, along with irritability and temper outbursts.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a parent whose 4-year-old child has autism spectrum disorder. Which instruction should the nurse include? A. "Change routines often so the child adapts." B. "Use long explanations to help the child understand." C. "Give the child plenty of notice before routines change." D. "Encourage the child to repeat the ritual behaviors for comfort."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reinforcing teaching with a parent whose 4-year-old child has autism spectrum disorder. Which instruction should the nurse include?

  • A. "Change routines often so the child adapts."
  • B. "Use long explanations to help the child understand."
  • C. "Give the child plenty of notice before routines change."
  • D. "Encourage the child to repeat the ritual behaviors for comfort."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Children with autism spectrum disorder need structured environments, short and concise communication, and plenty of notice before routine changes. Frequent changes and long explanations increase distress. The nurse should limit self-stimulating and ritualistic behaviors with alternative play activities.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the history of a 9-year-old who is fidgeting, interrupting others, and acting without considering consequences at home and at school. Which of the following is required for the diagnosis of ADHD? A. Symptoms present before age 12 in more than one setting B. Symptoms present only at school C. Symptoms beginning after age 12 D. Onset following a traumatic event
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the history of a 9-year-old who is fidgeting, interrupting others, and acting without considering consequences at home and at school. Which of the following is required for the diagnosis of ADHD?

  • A. Symptoms present before age 12 in more than one setting
  • B. Symptoms present only at school
  • C. Symptoms beginning after age 12
  • D. Onset following a traumatic event
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

ATI states ADHD behaviors must be present before age 12 and in more than one setting. A preceding traumatic event points to PTSD rather than ADHD. Symptoms limited to one setting do not meet criteria.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the charts of several clients. Which client is experiencing a maturational crisis? A. A client whose home was destroyed in a tornado B. A client who was laid off from work last week C. A client who retired after 35 years and cannot cope with the change D. A client who was assaulted while walking home
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the charts of several clients. Which client is experiencing a maturational crisis?

  • A. A client whose home was destroyed in a tornado
  • B. A client who was laid off from work last week
  • C. A client who retired after 35 years and cannot cope with the change
  • D. A client who was assaulted while walking home
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Maturational (internal) crises occur when a client reaches a new developmental stage that requires new coping mechanisms, such as retirement or marriage. A tornado and an assault are adventitious crises, and a job layoff is a situational (external) crisis.

cards.prompt: A nurse is planning care for a client in crisis. Which of the following actions should the nurse include? Select all that apply. A. Take an active, directive role. B. Assess for suicidal or homicidal ideation. C. Reassure the client that everything will be fine. D. Help the client set realistic, attainable goals. E. Delay addressing physical needs until the client is calm.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is planning care for a client in crisis. Which of the following actions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

  • A. Take an active, directive role.
  • B. Assess for suicidal or homicidal ideation.
  • C. Reassure the client that everything will be fine.
  • D. Help the client set realistic, attainable goals.
  • E. Delay addressing physical needs until the client is calm.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D

The nurse takes an active, directive role, monitors for suicide and homicide risk, and helps set realistic goals. False reassurance is nontherapeutic. Physical needs are addressed first, not delayed.

cards.prompt: A client who has been in a crisis for several days is pacing, cannot concentrate, and has tried several solutions that have failed. The client now reports feeling detached from reality and having thoughts of harming a coworker. Which phase of crisis is the client in, and what is the nurse's priority? A. Phase 2; teach relaxation techniques B. Phase 3; set short-term goals C. Phase 4; ensure safety of the client and coworker D. Phase 1; encourage use of defense mechanisms
cards.promptHtml:
A client who has been in a crisis for several days is pacing, cannot concentrate, and has tried several solutions that have failed. The client now reports feeling detached from reality and having thoughts of harming a coworker. Which phase of crisis is the client in, and what is the nurse's priority?

  • A. Phase 2; teach relaxation techniques
  • B. Phase 3; set short-term goals
  • C. Phase 4; ensure safety of the client and coworker
  • D. Phase 1; encourage use of defense mechanisms
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Phase 4 involves overwhelming anxiety with dissociative findings (depersonalization, detachment from reality) and possible violence against others or self. Safety comes first, and inpatient admission may be needed for homicidal thoughts. Goal setting and relaxation teaching come after the acute risk is addressed.

cards.prompt: A client is brought to a shelter after a flood destroyed the family home 2 days ago. The client denies thoughts of harming self or others, has not eaten or slept since the flood, and asks the nurse what to do next. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Teach the client a deep-breathing relaxation exercise. B. Help the client write a short-term action plan for finding housing. C. Give the client the number for a crisis warm line. D. Arrange for the client to have a meal and a place to rest.
cards.promptHtml:
A client is brought to a shelter after a flood destroyed the family home 2 days ago. The client denies thoughts of harming self or others, has not eaten or slept since the flood, and asks the nurse what to do next. Which action should the nurse take first?

  • A. Teach the client a deep-breathing relaxation exercise.
  • B. Help the client write a short-term action plan for finding housing.
  • C. Give the client the number for a crisis warm line.
  • D. Arrange for the client to have a meal and a place to rest.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Once safety has been screened (the client denies suicidal and homicidal thoughts), ATI directs the nurse to prioritize the client's physical needs first. Food and rest come before teaching relaxation, building a short-term action plan, or giving community resources, which are all appropriate later steps in crisis intervention.

cards.prompt: A nurse is talking with a client who lost their job last month and has major depressive disorder. Which of the following client statements should the nurse identify as overt comments about suicide? Select all that apply. A. "I've been thinking about taking all my pills at once." B. "Nothing ever seems to work out for me." C. "After I'm gone, nobody will have to worry about me anymore." D. "I keep thinking that dying would fix everything." E. "I don't see much point in planning for next year."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is talking with a client who lost their job last month and has major depressive disorder. Which of the following client statements should the nurse identify as overt comments about suicide? Select all that apply.

  • A. "I've been thinking about taking all my pills at once."
  • B. "Nothing ever seems to work out for me."
  • C. "After I'm gone, nobody will have to worry about me anymore."
  • D. "I keep thinking that dying would fix everything."
  • E. "I don't see much point in planning for next year."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D

Overt (direct) comments speak plainly about death, dying, or ending one's life. Statements that name a problem or a bleak outlook without mentioning death are covert (indirect) comments. Both types call for follow-up: the nurse should ask directly about suicidal thoughts and, for overt comments, assess for a plan.

cards.prompt: A client in the emergency department tells the nurse, "I'm going to end it tonight." Which question should the nurse ask first? A. "Do you have a way to do it, such as a gun or pills at home?" B. "How long have you been feeling this way?" C. "Who could you call for support tonight?" D. "What has been going on at work lately?"
cards.promptHtml:
A client in the emergency department tells the nurse, "I'm going to end it tonight." Which question should the nurse ask first?

  • A. "Do you have a way to do it, such as a gun or pills at home?"
  • B. "How long have you been feeling this way?"
  • C. "Who could you call for support tonight?"
  • D. "What has been going on at work lately?"
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

The greatest risk is that the client will act on a plan. The priority assessment is how detailed and lethal the plan is and whether the client has access to the means. Duration of feelings, support system, and stressors are useful data but come after the plan and access to means are assessed.

cards.prompt: A nurse is assigned to one-on-one observation of a client on suicide precautions. Which action is appropriate? A. Search the client's belongings while the client is at group therapy. B. Record the client's location, mood, statements, and behavior every 15 min. C. Allow the client to sleep with the blanket pulled over both hands. D. Let the client shower alone with the door closed because the rod is breakaway.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is assigned to one-on-one observation of a client on suicide precautions. Which action is appropriate?

  • A. Search the client's belongings while the client is at group therapy.
  • B. Record the client's location, mood, statements, and behavior every 15 min.
  • C. Allow the client to sleep with the blanket pulled over both hands.
  • D. Let the client shower alone with the door closed because the rod is breakaway.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

ATI has the nurse record the client's whereabouts, mood, statements in the client's own words, and behavior at 15-minute intervals or as the facility requires. Belongings are searched while the client is there, the client's hands stay in view even when asleep, and constant one-on-one supervision means the client is never out of sight.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing facility policy on no-suicide contracts. For which client is a no-suicide contract discouraged? A. A client who has depression, has built trust with the nurse, and is preparing for discharge B. A client who has an adjustment disorder and is attending outpatient follow-up C. A client brought to the emergency department who is intoxicated and very agitated D. A client who has bipolar disorder in remission and asks for a written safety agreement
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing facility policy on no-suicide contracts. For which client is a no-suicide contract discouraged?

  • A. A client who has depression, has built trust with the nurse, and is preparing for discharge
  • B. A client who has an adjustment disorder and is attending outpatient follow-up
  • C. A client brought to the emergency department who is intoxicated and very agitated
  • D. A client who has bipolar disorder in remission and asks for a written safety agreement
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

A no-suicide contract has no legal force and must not take the place of other safety measures. ATI advises against using one when the client is in crisis, intoxicated, psychotic, highly impulsive, or very angry or agitated. In a stable therapeutic relationship it can help build and keep trust.

cards.prompt: During a community meeting on an inpatient unit, which client statement should the nurse identify as aggressive communication? A. "I'm frustrated that my pass was canceled today." B. "Keep talking and see what happens to you." C. "I get upset when people take my seat." D. "I would like a turn to speak now."
cards.promptHtml:
During a community meeting on an inpatient unit, which client statement should the nurse identify as aggressive communication?

  • A. "I'm frustrated that my pass was canceled today."
  • B. "Keep talking and see what happens to you."
  • C. "I get upset when people take my seat."
  • D. "I would like a turn to speak now."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Aggressive communication implies a threat toward, or disrespect for, another person. Option B carries an implied threat. The other statements describe the client's own feelings or make a request without threatening or demeaning anyone, which is a healthy way to express anger.

cards.prompt: A client on an inpatient unit is becoming increasingly agitated. Which interventions are less restrictive options the nurse should try before restraint is considered? Select all that apply. A. Offer the client a prescribed as-needed medication. B. Reduce noise and stimulation around the client. C. Apply wrist restraints as a precaution. D. Provide one-to-one supervision. E. Place the client in seclusion until calm.
cards.promptHtml:
A client on an inpatient unit is becoming increasingly agitated. Which interventions are less restrictive options the nurse should try before restraint is considered? Select all that apply.

  • A. Offer the client a prescribed as-needed medication.
  • B. Reduce noise and stimulation around the client.
  • C. Apply wrist restraints as a precaution.
  • D. Provide one-to-one supervision.
  • E. Place the client in seclusion until calm.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D

Seclusion and restraint are a last resort, used per legal guidelines only after less restrictive options fail and there is a risk of harm. ATI lists verbal interventions, an as-needed medication, decreased environmental stimulation, close observation, and one-to-one supervision as the less restrictive options to try first.

cards.prompt: A client is standing in the hallway shouting at a peer, leaning forward with clenched fists. Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic? A. "Why are you yelling at him like that?" B. "Stop that right now or you are going to seclusion." C. "I need you to lower your voice and walk with me to the courtyard so we can talk." D. "Tell me what happened in your childhood that makes you this angry."
cards.promptHtml:
A client is standing in the hallway shouting at a peer, leaning forward with clenched fists. Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?

  • A. "Why are you yelling at him like that?"
  • B. "Stop that right now or you are going to seclusion."
  • C. "I need you to lower your voice and walk with me to the courtyard so we can talk."
  • D. "Tell me what happened in your childhood that makes you this angry."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Calm, direct limit setting that tells the client exactly what to do, paired with physical activity such as walking, helps de-escalate anger. "Why" questions sound critical and cause defensiveness, threats escalate the situation, and probing for deep history is inappropriate while the client is escalating.

cards.prompt: A nurse is administering haloperidol to a client who has been aggressive. Which instruction should the nurse include? A. "Limit time in the sun and wear sunscreen and sunglasses." B. "Limit your fluid intake to prevent swelling." C. "Decrease the fiber in your diet." D. "You may stop the medication when you feel calm."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is administering haloperidol to a client who has been aggressive. Which instruction should the nurse include?

  • A. "Limit time in the sun and wear sunscreen and sunglasses."
  • B. "Limit your fluid intake to prevent swelling."
  • C. "Decrease the fiber in your diet."
  • D. "You may stop the medication when you feel calm."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Haloperidol can cause photosensitivity, dry mouth, constipation, and orthostatic hypotension. ATI teaching is to limit sunlight and wear sunscreen and sunglasses, take frequent sips of water, and increase fiber (a stool softener may be needed). The nurse also keeps the client hydrated and tests for muscle rigidity because of the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the cycle of violence with a newly licensed nurse. Which statement by the newly licensed nurse indicates understanding? A. "The acute battering phase lasts longer than the other phases." B. "In the tension-building phase, the vulnerable person usually blames the perpetrator." C. "Without intervention, the time between violent episodes gets longer." D. "In the honeymoon phase, the perpetrator acts loving and promises to change."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the cycle of violence with a newly licensed nurse. Which statement by the newly licensed nurse indicates understanding?

  • A. "The acute battering phase lasts longer than the other phases."
  • B. "In the tension-building phase, the vulnerable person usually blames the perpetrator."
  • C. "Without intervention, the time between violent episodes gets longer."
  • D. "In the honeymoon phase, the perpetrator acts loving and promises to change."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

In the honeymoon phase the perpetrator is sorry, loving, and promises change, and the vulnerable person hopes for it before the cycle starts again. Acute battering is the most violent and shortest phase. In tension-building the vulnerable person tends to accept the blame, and without intervention the periods between episodes become shorter.

cards.prompt: A nurse at a pediatric clinic is examining a 5-year-old child. Which findings should the nurse recognize as possible indications of abuse? Select all that apply. A. Burns in a stocking pattern on both feet B. Several bruises on the shins C. Welts shaped like a belt buckle on the buttocks D. A human bite mark on the upper arm E. Scraped elbows
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse at a pediatric clinic is examining a 5-year-old child. Which findings should the nurse recognize as possible indications of abuse? Select all that apply.

  • A. Burns in a stocking pattern on both feet
  • B. Several bruises on the shins
  • C. Welts shaped like a belt buckle on the buttocks
  • D. A human bite mark on the upper arm
  • E. Scraped elbows
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, C, D

Stocking or glove burns suggest forced immersion in boiling water, object-shaped welts and bruising on the buttocks suggest beatings, and human bite marks are an abuse indicator. Bruises and scrapes on the arms and legs are expected from play in preschool through adolescent age groups.

cards.prompt: A client who is 20 weeks pregnant reports that her partner pushed her down the stairs. She tells the nurse she plans to leave him tonight. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Give her information about parenting classes. B. Teach her relaxation techniques for stress. C. Help her develop a safety plan that includes a safe place to go. D. Suggest communication courses she could take with her partner.
cards.promptHtml:
A client who is 20 weeks pregnant reports that her partner pushed her down the stairs. She tells the nurse she plans to leave him tonight. Which action should the nurse take first?

  • A. Give her information about parenting classes.
  • B. Teach her relaxation techniques for stress.
  • C. Help her develop a safety plan that includes a safe place to go.
  • D. Suggest communication courses she could take with her partner.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Pregnancy increases the likelihood of partner violence, and the vulnerable person is at greatest risk when trying to leave. The greatest risk is injury from further abuse, so the priority is a safety plan with safe places to live. Education, stress management, and therapy referrals are appropriate later.

cards.prompt: A nurse is collecting data from a 2-month-old infant who is irritable and has a bulging fontanel and an increasing head circumference. Which action should the nurse take? A. Reassure the parents that these findings are expected at this age. B. Report suspected abuse as required by law once the infant receives medical care. C. Delay documenting until the parents explain the findings. D. Enroll the parents in a parenting class before further assessment.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is collecting data from a 2-month-old infant who is irritable and has a bulging fontanel and an increasing head circumference. Which action should the nurse take?

  • A. Reassure the parents that these findings are expected at this age.
  • B. Report suspected abuse as required by law once the infant receives medical care.
  • C. Delay documenting until the parents explain the findings.
  • D. Enroll the parents in a parenting class before further assessment.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Bulging fontanels and increasing head circumference suggest shaken baby syndrome with intracranial hemorrhage. The infant needs urgent care, and all states require nurses to report suspected child abuse, with civil and criminal penalties for failing to report. Data are documented as collected, and parenting classes are a later teaching point.
